tasks.title: Complete direct LTE MQTT transport: CIPSEND prompt and CONNACK parsing
tasks.description: The socket opens but the MQTT CONNECT is never confirmed. Two known defects: (1) AT+CIPSEND emits a '>' prompt that may not be newline-terminated, so a line-based reader blocks until timeout; (2) broker CONNACK bytes such as 20 02 00 00 are not newline-terminated, so a line parser cannot read them. Replace the line reader with a byte-level reader that recognises the '>' prompt and reads fixed-length CONNACK. Consider migrating to the installed TinyGSM A7672x client, which already uses CIPOPEN correctly.
acceptance_criteria: Device logs MQTT-CONNECT sent
A CONNACK is received and parsed (expect 0x20 0x02 0x00 0x00)
A telemetry payload is observed by an independent subscriber on the target cluster
No bridge, tunnel, relay or cloudflared is involved at any point

tasks.title: LBS fallback integration into the location service
tasks.description: Wrap the proven AT+CLBS=1,1 call. Preconditions: patch antenna attached and AT+SIMEI populated from AT+CGSN. Populate the position immediately from LBS, then upgrade to the GNSS fix when it arrives. Record the accuracy radius with the fix and mark the source as LBS or GPS.
acceptance_criteria: Position available within seconds of boot, before any GNSS fix
Position source is explicitly recorded as LBS or GNSS
Accuracy radius is carried through to telemetry
Longitude is not confused with latitude (CLBS returns lon first)

tasks.title: GNSS service with uninterrupted cold-start handling
tasks.description: Bring up the GNSS engine once per boot, keep it powered, and parse NMEA with TinyGPS++. The existing tracker sketch has a counter bug: its '15 minute' loop increments an integer by 1000 per iteration, so it exits after seconds. Use a millis() deadline.
acceptance_criteria: A real millis()-based deadline is used, not an iteration counter
Fix quality 1 with satsUsed > 0 is required before reporting a GNSS position
The module is not power-cycled mid-session

tasks.title: Choose and document the firmware framework baseline (ESP-IDF vs Arduino)
tasks.description: The PRD allows either ESP-IDF 5.x or Arduino-ESP32 3.x. All working hardware baselines today are Arduino sketches; nomad-sentinel is an ESP-IDF project with MODEM_USE_UART 0 and blocked SD. Every remaining verified capability (NAT via esp32_nat_router, esp_camera, ESP-SR, esp-mqtt) is a first-class ESP-IDF citizen. This decision blocks TASK-101, TASK-103 and TASK-104 and must be made first.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded as an ADR with alternatives and consequences
Rationale addresses NAT/routing feasibility on each framework
Migration cost for the existing Arduino baselines is stated

verification.verified_by: ESP32-S3_A7670E_4G_LTE hardware run, Arduino ESP32 core 3.3.11
verification.reason: PPP negotiated end to end on the Airtel SIM. lwIP reached phase RUNNING with local=100.76.140.112, gateway=10.64.64.64, mtu=1500, up=1, and held it stable (217 bytes out / 235 bytes in). A cold-boot run with no USB unplug reproduced it at local=100.77.131.255 (230 bytes out / 273 bytes in). See TEST-020 for the full capture.
